text:
Tyson Kozak is healthy, and Buffalo is leaning on him. Buffalo Hockey Beat ran a headline this month saying he's playing some of his best hockey, and the Niagara Gazette wrote that a healthy Kozak is making his presence felt.

He's a seventh-round pick from 2021 who plays about 11 minutes a night as a checking center, and Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best players last season (98th percentile competition). That's a hard job for a 23-year-old.

The numbers reflect it. Buffalo gets 43% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about seven points worse than without him. He has one goal and four points in 15 games, three assists in his last ten.

NHL Edge has his top speed at the 91st percentile. His shot is near the bottom of the league, and he's taken only six. What to watch: whether the checking role produces better on-ice results as Buffalo tries to turn around a 1-3-1 stretch.
